IL services are provided in person with the trainer and customer at the same location. IL services within this chapter cannot be provided remotely.

An Applicant applying for a contract must comply with the following VR-SFP Manual chapters in addition to the OE SOW.

2.2 VR STANDARDS FOR PROVIDERS (VR-SFP) MANUAL The VR Standards for Providers (VR-SFP) Manual focuses on the business practices, processes, and policies that must be followed for TWC and the Provider to comply with federal and state laws and TWC rules and requirements.
Each Provider is contractually responsible for maintaining compliance with the most current VR-SFP Manual.
All Providers should subscribe to TWC GovDelivery list to gain these notifications.

All IL skills trainers must have accomplished the following: Earned a bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university with a concentration in rehabilitation, education, psychology, sociology, or a related field and obtained: one year of work experience in rehabilitation teaching, rehabilitation, or education of people with disabilities, or two years' work experience in general education or other related field; and Presented written and/or hands-on training sessions on IL skills.
Sessions must be observed and determined qualified by the ILS-OIB program specialist's designee.
The IL skills provider must make the initial contact with a customer who is referred for independent living skills training within 15 working days of the referral.
The application assessment must be completed within one to two hours of the initial contact.

The initial contact and application assessment must be conducted individually and must be documented using the following forms: VR5051, Application for Services; VR5053, Application Statement—ILS-OIB; VR5060, Permission to Collect Information; VR5061, Notice and Consent for Disclosure of Personal Information; VR2891, Customer Services Report: ILS-OIB Progress Report
The IL skills provider must contact a customer who is referred for a comprehensive assessment within 30 calendar days of the referral.

The IL skills provider must document the comprehensive assessment on VR2954, Comprehensive Assessment for Independent Living Program. The recommendations section of the form must list the IL skills training sessions and services that the IL skills provider has identified for inclusion in the customer's ILP.
The monthly progress report (VR2891) must: detail the services provided to the customer; document the outcome of each service; and include any recommendations for changes to the ILP.
Services must not begin until a service authorization has been issued.

Providers must have written authorization from ILS-OIB before providing services to a customer. If a service is provided before a service authorization is issued by ILS-OIB and received by the provider, ILS-OIB will not authorize payment for the service.

Open Enrollment No. 3202600157 OE for Independent Living Services for Older Individuals who are Blind The IL skills provider must document the comprehensive assessment on VR2954, Comprehensive Assessment for Independent Living Program.

To facilitate payment after the assessment and/or training period, the provider of IL skills services submits the following (as applicable) at least every 35 days, using clear and descriptive terms: VR5053, Application Statement—ILS-OIB; VR2954, Comprehensive Assessment for Independent Living Program; VR2891, Customer Services Report: ILS-OIB Progress Report

ILS-OIB Progress Report—at the end of the assessment and/or training period The information entered must demonstrate the following: • Attendance was recorded (include the total number of hours that the customer participated in services). • All necessary accommodations were provided, compensatory techniques were used, and special needs were met for the customer to successfully participate in the services. • The customers’ performance, skills, and needs were assessed and the results summarized for the reporting period. • The goals and objectives were measurable and established for all skills to be addressed. • A projected timeline, including training hours, was established for each goal.
VR-SFP Manual Chapter 3: Basic Standards require each Provider to run background checks on each Provider staff member who will interact with any VR Customer.
Background checks must be completed by the Provider before the Provider staff interacts with any VR Customer.

Applicants and Providers are responsible for obtaining a background check for all applicable Provider staff. A background check consists of running a name-based search from the Texas Department of Public Safety and checking the National Public Sex Offender public website.

However, if a Provider (or Provider's staff or Provider's subcontractors) do transport a VR Customer in the Provider's vehicle or Provider's staff personal vehicle, they must meet the minimum liability requirements of the Texas Department of Insurance. The Provider must maintain current proof of insurance for any Provider staff who transports VR Customers.

When Provider staff transports VR Customers in personal vehicles, the Provider staff must submit to VR proof of auto liability insurance as required by the Texas Department of Insurance with Form VR3455.
Verification statements on Form VR3455 must be signed by the Provider staff represented on the form and the Provider's Director appointed by the legal authorized representative.
The Provider must maintain current proof of insurance for any Provider staff who transports VR Customers.

Each Provider/Entity must have a Director who meets the qualification as stated in the VR-SFP Manual, Chapter 3 Basic Standards. The Provider's/Entity's legally authorized representative must appoint Director(s) using Form VR3441A. The Provider's/Entity's Director must also have a VR 3455 included in the Application.
For any service selected by the Applicant on VR3441B, the Applicant must have at least one (1) person who meets the qualifications to provide the service(s) as described in Article II Scope of Work.
Each Provider staff must have VR3455 with the supporting documentation (resumes, transcripts, proof of insurance, and credentials) included in the Application.

After contract award, a VR3455 with supporting documentation must be submitted for each person who will be providing services under the Contract. Each Provider must submit Form VR3455 and the supporting evidence that the staff member meets the required qualifications within 30 days of: hiring new staff member; making a significant change to a staff member's job duties...; changing staff qualifications and/or credentials; or terminating a staff member.

6.9 REQUIRED INSURANCE Providers are responsible for their actions and the actions of their employees and subcontractors.

6.10 FAILURE TO PERFORM If the Provider fails to perform in accordance with the provisions of the contract, TWC may upon written notice to the Provider, take adverse action against the Provider, up to and including terminating the Contract in whole or in part. If notice of termination is given, all work by the Provider shall cease on the effective date of the termination, and TWC will not pay for work performed on or after the effective date of termination.

The Provider and any of its subcontractors associated with the Contract will remedy in a timely manner any weaknesses, deficiencies, or program noncompliance found as a result of a review, audit or investigation, and any performance or fiscal exceptions found by TWC, the SAO, the federal funding agency, their successor agencies, or any of their duly authorized representatives.

During the term of the Contract or any extension or renewal thereof, the Provider shall notify TWC in writing of any substantial change in the ownership or control of the Provider as soon as possible, but no later than thirty (30) days prior to its occurrence.
Provider must also notify TWC in writing of any change in financial condition as soon as possible, but no later than ten (10) days after its occurrence.
